subject: Frishberg et al. (2014)
object: Frishberg et al. (2014) reported 2 brothers, born to consanguineous healthy parents of Arab descent, who were evaluated for psychomotor delay associated with a triple-A-like syndrome (anisocoria, alacrima, and achalasia). The proband had markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion, with normal excretion of oxalate, citrate, and glycerate. Abdominal ultrasound showed normal-sized kidneys with normal echotexture. The authors found that the genetic cause of the triple-A-like syndrome in this family was unrelated to the metabolic abnormality, and they described the glycolic aciduria as isolated and asymptomatic.

subject: Frishberg et al. (2014)
object: In a patient of Arab descent with isolated glycolic aciduria, born to consanguineous parents, Frishberg et al. (2014) used direct sequencing of the HAO1 gene and identified a homozygous splice-site mutation (c.814-1G>C) at the invariant -1 position of the intron 5 splice acceptor site. HAO1 is expressed specifically in the liver, so the authors tested the mutation with an in vitro hybrid-minigene assay. Cells transfected with the mutant minigene produced an abnormal splice variant. The authors concluded that expression of a defective glycolate oxidase splice variant causes isolated asymptomatic glycolic aciduria.

subject: Frishberg et al. (2014)
object: Frishberg et al. (2014) suggested that the observation that loss of glycolate oxidase causes only asymptomatic glycolic aciduria supports developing substrate reduction as a new treatment approach for primary hyperoxaluria type I.

subject: McGregor et al. (2020)
object: McGregor et al. (2020) described a healthy British-Pakistani woman in her fifth decade who carried a lifelong complete HAO1 knockout. She was identified by exome sequencing of autozygous population cohorts (Born in Bradford and Genes and Health). She was overweight (BMI 30-35 kg/m2) and the mother of 3 healthy children. A renal ultrasound was normal, and apart from common short-term illnesses she was otherwise healthy. The authors concluded that lifelong HAO1 knockout was safe and without clinical phenotype in this woman.

subject: McGregor et al. (2020)
object: In the HAO1-null woman, McGregor et al. (2020) found plasma glycolate of 171 nmol/mL (reference 14 or less), about 12 times the upper limit of normal. Her urinary glycolate/creatinine ratio was 199 to 309 mg/g (reference 50 or less), about 6 times the upper limit of normal. Plasma and urinary oxalate, plasma glycerate, the serum anion gap and standard serum biochemistries were all normal.

subject: McGregor et al. (2020)
object: McGregor et al. (2020) profiled 1,871 plasma metabolites and lipids in the woman and compared them with 25 controls. Of these, 18 biochemicals, including glycolate, were markedly elevated (more than 5 SD above controls). Unconjugated bile acids were elevated and glycine- and taurine-conjugated bile acids were reduced, which the authors suggested might reflect reduced local availability of glycine. Six of the elevated metabolites had structures compatible with being potential HAO1 substrates.

subject: McGregor et al. (2020)
object: In the woman, McGregor et al. (2020) identified a homozygous 1-bp deletion in the HAO1 gene (c.997delC, rs1186715161), predicted to cause a frameshift (Leu333SerfsTer4) that truncates the final 37 amino acids. The variant was found by exome sequencing of blood DNA and confirmed by Sanger sequencing of saliva DNA. It lay within a 5.2-Mb autozygous region, and she was not homozygous for any other rare predicted loss-of-function variant. No homozygous predicted loss-of-function HAO1 variants were present in gnomAD v2.1.

subject: HAO1 c.997delc / p.L333Sfs / p.L333fs
object: HAO1

subject: McGregor et al. (2020)
object: McGregor et al. (2020) expressed the p.Leu333SerfsTer4 HAO1 variant in CHO-K1 cells. The variant protein was markedly reduced and diffusely mislocalised, whereas mRNA levels were unaffected. The authors linked this to loss of the C-terminal SKI peroxisomal targeting tripeptide. Using lumasiran phase 1 data from healthy volunteers for comparison, they estimated that the woman retained less than 2% residual glycolate oxidase activity.

subject: McGregor et al. (2020)
object: McGregor et al. (2020) reported that about 1 in 2,700 individuals in gnomAD v2.1 is heterozygous for an HAO1 predicted loss-of-function variant. They estimated that the expected frequency of homozygotes in an outbred population is about 1 in 30 million.

subject: McGregor et al. (2020)
object: McGregor et al. (2020) concluded that the clinically silent lifelong HAO1 knockout supports the potential safety of chronic HAO1 inhibition, such as with the RNAi therapeutic lumasiran, for treating primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
